newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Monorchio says Feb accounts looking good.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Monorchio says Feb accounts looking good.

text.p: Italian state auditor Andrea Monorchio said on Wednesday that public finances were in good shape in February but declined to comment on the upcoming mini-budget until official data are published March 15 and 30.
"It seems that (the accounts) went well in February," Monorchio told reporters in response to questions about Italy's forthcoming mini-budget.

He said that Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi had already said that the official data would be published in the last two weeks of March. "On that date I will be able to say the size of the mini-budget," he said.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has repeatedly said he will wait for publication of the state accounts before announcing how big the supplementary finance package will be.

But he said last week that Italy was currently some 6.0-14 trillion lire ($3.6-8.4 billion) short of achieving the key goal of bringing its deficit to three percent of Gross Domestic Product that is a condition for single European currency entry.
The mini-budget is widely expected to contain up to 15 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures.
